Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book and SLOOS:
- FOMC tone (July 26, 2017): Labor market continues to strengthen; economic activity rising at a moderate pace; inflation running below 2% and monitored closely; policy remains accommodative with gradualism and balance sheet normalization “relatively soon.”
- Beige Book cross-check (June 2017): Economic activity expanded across Federal Reserve Districts; consumer spending rising; labor markets tight for both low- and high-skilled workers with reported shortages; wages trending up; energy activity improved with oil and natural gas. These observations reinforce the FOMC’s view of solid labor conditions and moderate growth.
- SLOOS cross-check (July 2017): Weaker loan demand across CRE and consumer credit (auto, credit card), with tighter standards for consumer loans; mortgage standards eased in several categories (jumbo, QM, GSE) while home-purchase and HELOC standards largely unchanged; foreign banks tightened C&I and CRE despite stronger CRE demand abroad. This points to modest headwinds for consumption and investment.
- Implication: Beige Book strength in activity and labor offsets some of the SLOOS softness, but below-target inflation and tighter consumer credit conditions keep the overall tone cautious. Net read remains mildly positive, supported by tight labor and rising consumer spending, tempered by softer credit dynamics.
